extracted.intended_audience: vocational administrators and faculty (vocational education teachers and vocational directors)
extracted.subtask_description: Final report on a workshop designed to develop vocational educators' knowledge and skills for preparing effective funding proposals; summarizes objectives, outcomes, problems encountered, and recommendations for future workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop knowledge and skills to prepare effective proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The workshop aimed to help participants develop the knowledge and skills needed to prepare effective proposals for vocational education funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad program objective: training should cover both conceptual understanding and practical skills necessary to produce fundable proposals; success measured by participants' demonstrated ability to prepare proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform participants about funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should be informed about available funding sources for vocational education, especially federal funds which have increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should include overview of funding programs, eligibility, priorities, and typical funder expectations so participants can identify appropriate opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain what is involved in applying for funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop should teach participants what is involved in the application process for funding (procedural and substantive requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include application components, timelines, submission procedures, required documentation, and administrative steps; practical walkthroughs or examples are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach how to express the application in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should learn how to express their application effectively in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize clear, persuasive proposal-writing skills: articulating objectives, methods, budgets, justification, and aligning language to funder criteria and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants should bring project ideas to the workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective workshops expect participants to bring concrete project ideas that can be developed into proposals during the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: most participants brought no ideas, which limited skill development. Pre-workshop assignments or solicitation of project concepts recommended to ensure productive hands-on work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide incentives such as college credit to encourage participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering college credit (or similar incentives) can encourage participation; in this workshop six of nineteen participants sought and were granted credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider structuring workshop for credit or certification to increase commitment and follow-through among attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for logistical contingencies and adequate preplanning
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops must include thorough preplanning and contingency plans to avoid disruptions (e.g., severe weather) that can curtail sessions and reduce effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation from the report: change preplanning procedures for future workshops to ensure objectives can be met despite external disruptions; implies scheduling, materials, participant readiness, and backup plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure workshop effectiveness by outcomes, not just enthusiasm
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation should distinguish participant enthusiasm from actual achievement of workshop objectives (skills gained, proposal drafts produced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although participants were enthusiastic, most objectives were not achieved; use outcome-based assessment (e.g., number of usable proposal drafts, demonstrated skills) to judge success.
